registry_info.name: facture_bench
registry_info.description: A synthesis artifact for the `facture` family (5 registry names, 4 vocabularies, 9 pooled terms, 1 term in common). One lathed capsule restated on one deck in every state of making the family can be said to share, with the row emptying as the requirement to share gets stricter.
registry_info.note: Per-token registry file so parallel builders never share one JSON. The `facture` word and the nine pooled terms are COMPUTED at runtime from the five members' own FACTURES consts and checked in both directions at _ready; the `resolution` values and their four segment counts are read from sphere_mid.RESOLUTION. Do not retype either here or in the script. Neither of the two axes declared below is the family word - see dna.declines.

facture_bench.name: Facture Bench
facture_bench.description: One lathed capsule - the body the word `facture` was coined on - standing up to five times on a single deck, each copy in a different state of its own making: poured with no seam and no count, wired down to the edge graph, cut into countable planes, opened by a quarter-section, and given a wall of slabs with visible rims. The form, the size, the pad and the deck are identical at every station; only what the copy admits about its own construction differs. The five terms are not typed in: they are computed at build time from the five family members' own FACTURES consts, ordered by how many members declare them. `quorum` sets how many members must agree before a term may stand - at two the deck holds five bodies, at five it holds one, and the one is `cast`. `resolution` is sphere_mid's own word and its own ladder of 4, 7, 16 and 32 segments, and it is the axis that decides whether the making can be hidden at all.
interactions: walk the deck and find the one body that never changes when the mould gets finer
set quorum=all and count the empty pads - that is how much of a shared vocabulary the family actually has
set resolution=ultra and try to tell the cut body from the poured one
set resolution=coarse and watch every station start confessing at once
stand at the fourth and fifth pads: they are the only place in this corpus where `section` and `shell` have ever been in the same frame
facture_bench.qfep_connection: A vocabulary that looks shared because every speaker uses one of its words. Five objects declare `facture` and no two declare the same list; what they all agree on is `cast`, which is the value that does nothing - an early return before the axis begins. The commons is real at exactly one point, and that point is the absence of a claim. The bench does not resolve this into a canon; it stands the pool at every threshold of agreement and lets the deck empty, because a vocabulary forced into one list would be a fact about the forcing. What is foreclosed is named in dna.declines: four words that only one object each has ever needed, left off the deck on purpose and written down instead.
facture_bench.relationships: synthesis over the five registry names that declare `facture` - capsule, dome, folded_strip, platonic_grabbables, triangleprofiles. It re-runs none of their axes and replaces none of them, and it adopts the word by exhibiting it rather than sweeping it, as taxonomy_hall does with `taxonomy` and instruction_bench with `tell`. Its second axis is borrowed whole from sphere_mid, the primitives tier's own word for how finely a body is cut; dna.note (5) records that sphere_high and sphere_low's `facets` is a sixth member of the facture pool under another name.

spatial_needs.footprint_note: The deck is 1.98 m across five slots by 0.40 m deep and 0.368 m tall to the top of the standing body. It is a walk-along exhibit read left to right, so the clearance in front is what the artifact actually needs.

measurements.measured_by: computed from the script's own layout constants, re-derived in a Python replica of the geometry and rasterised at the sweep camera; no Godot was run, per the brief. MeshInstance3D only, which here is everything the artifact builds.

dna.axis_shape:
`quorum` NESTS STRICTLY, and provably rather than by inspection: raising a frequency threshold can only remove terms, so the standing set at each value is a subset of the set at the value before it - {cast, armature, facet, section, shell} > {cast, armature, facet} > {cast, armature} > {cast}. The four values are therefore an ordered sequence and must be swept in order; trimming its tail lowers the ceiling of the ladder and loses no case.

`resolution` is a MONOTONE MAGNITUDE - one integer, 4 / 7 / 16 / 32, read from sphere_mid.RESOLUTION. Its values neither contain one another as sets nor sit side by side as parallel alternatives; they are four samples of a scalar, and trimming its tail removes the fine end, which is where the closest pair lives. Both are named because they call for opposite handling under trimming, and because `resolution` is declared SECOND for exactly that reason (Law 16): build_dna_gallery trims the later axis from the tail, so a capped run drops `ultra` then `fine`, which is the predicted closest pair rather than the default.

THE FAMILY WORD `facture` IS NEITHER, WHICH IS WHY IT IS NOT AN AXIS HERE - see dna.declines. Read out of the members' code it is MIXED: capsule.gd::_armature() walks the edges of the same triangle list _facet() shades and draws no faces, so `armature` is `facet` with the skin SUBTRACTED and `cast` is `facet` with the partition subtracted - two complements inside a third - while `shell` (folded_strip.gd::_prism, a per-face extrusion with rims) and `section` (capsule.gd::_section, a clip plus a filled cut face) are PARALLEL apparatus that sit on no ladder at all.
dna.default:
quorum=two, resolution=mid. A SYNTHESIS HAS NO SHIPPED PLACEMENTS, so there is nothing to preserve and the default is a free design choice; the rule that outranks everything in doc/DNA_PROMOTION_BRIEF.md governs promotions of PLACED artifacts and has no work to do here. That freedom was spent on the strongest single reading.

WHY `two` AND NOT `all` OR `three`. `two` is the pool as the corpus actually holds it - every term that more than one member uses - and it is the only value at which the whole argument is visible at once: five states of making, one body, with `section` and `shell` standing beside each other for the first and only time in this corpus. `all` is the loudest single claim on the bench and the emptiest picture: one body and four bare pads, which is a punchline rather than an opening. `three` loses precisely the two terms that carry finding (3), so a visitor meeting it first would never see the solid/surface split that explains why the family has no common list. Two is also second in the declared order and therefore survives any cap of 2 or more.

WHY `mid` AND NOT `coarse`. `mid` is 7 segments - sphere_mid's own default, and the rung nearest the 5 radial segments capsule actually ships, so the bench opens on the tessellation the family itself works at. `coarse` is 4, which turns a body of revolution into a square prism: it is the loudest tile on the resolution axis and it prejudges the axis by making its own coarse end absurd. At `mid` all five stations are separately legible - facet cells 28.2 px, wire tubes 5.0 px against 89.8 px edges, shell rims splaying 2.18 px - and the argument that fineness hides making is still ahead of the visitor rather than already made.
dna.was: did not exist. Nothing was promoted here and no shipped behaviour was touched; capsule, dome, folded_strip, platonic_grabbables and triangleprofiles are read and not modified. This is the cross-member argument the five `facture` declarations leave unbuilt. Every one of them spends the word in a single mutually-exclusive branch - capsule.gd's `match facture:` after an early return, dome.gd's `_apply_facture()` after `_restore_baseline()`, folded_strip.gd's `if facture != "facet": _apply_facture()` - so no member can stand two states of its own making at the same time, and none of them has ever photographed two of the pool's terms in one frame. Four of the nine pooled terms have no second member to be compared against at all.
dna.note:
THE ARGUMENT, AND WHY IT NEEDS A BENCH RATHER THAN A MEMBER.

`facture` is how a thing was made, which is a claim a finished object usually hides. Five registry names declare the word and no two of them declare the same list:

    capsule               cast . facet . armature . section . wear
    dome                  cast . blank . core . section
    folded_strip          facet . cast . armature . shell
    platonic_grabbables   plate . cast . armature
    triangleprofiles      facet . cast . armature . shell

    pooled: cast 5, armature 4, facet 3, section 2, shell 2, wear/blank/core/plate 1 each

That is the shape doc/reports/VOCABULARY_SPLIT.md ruled on for `support`: a POOL rather than a disagreement, each object declaring the states of making it can honestly take. The cost, stated there and paid here, is that the word cannot be swept across its family, because there is no common list to vary. So the bench EXHIBITS it - all of it standing at once on one deck, one body, one size, one pad - and varies the pool's own threshold instead. Every station on the deck is a term some member of the family has committed to.

WHAT IT FOUND, all of it read out of the members' code before anything was built.

(1) THE ONE TERM EVERY MEMBER SHARES IS THE ONE THAT REQUIRES NO IMPLEMENTATION. `cast` is the only word in all five lists, and in capsule.gd it is `if facture == "cast": return` placed before the script reads the mesh, touches a material or adds a node; in dome.gd it is the same early return before a single CSG operand is moved. It is not a state of making that four other states are alternatives to - it is the scene BEFORE the axis, and the family agreed on it because agreeing on it cost nothing.

(2) EVERY MEMBER DECLARES ITS OWN UNTOUCHED SCENE FIRST, so all five declaration orders are default hoists - and the five defaults are not the same word. capsule and dome ship `cast`, folded_strip and triangleprofiles ship `facet` (their legacy path is the one that falls through, not the one named cast), platonic_grabbables ships `plate`. THE FAMILY DISAGREES ABOUT WHAT AN OBJECT LOOKS LIKE WHEN NOBODY HAS SAID ANYTHING ABOUT HOW IT WAS MADE: poured, or counted, or drawn and filled at once. That disagreement is invisible in any one member and is the first thing the leftmost three pads of this bench put side by side.

(3) THE POOL SPLITS ALONG SOLID VERSUS SURFACE, AND THAT IS WHY THERE IS NO COMMON LIST. `section` appears on exactly the two members whose subject is a SOLID (capsule's capsule, dome's boolean block) and `shell` on exactly the two whose subject is a SURFACE (folded_strip's ribbon, triangleprofiles' pleated wall). A solid can be cut open to show that it has an inside; a sheet can be given a wall it does not have. Neither operation is available to the other kind of body, so no member could ever have carried both terms. This bench's body is a lathed SOLID drawn as an explicit tessellation, which is the one subject that can honestly take both - and the bench is therefore the only place in the corpus where `section` and `shell` have ever stood beside each other.

(4) platonic_grabbables' LIST IS SHORT BECAUSE OF ITS MECHANISM, NOT ITS SUBJECT. Its _apply() writes exactly one property - MeshInstance3D.material_override - and never rebuilds geometry, so its three values are precisely the three that a material swap can express. A dodecahedron could obviously be sectioned or shelled; the artifact cannot, because it declined to touch a mesh. A vocabulary bounded by an implementation reads identically in the registry to a vocabulary bounded by an argument.

(5) THE POOL IS WIDER THAN FIVE MEMBERS, BECAUSE ONE OF ITS QUESTIONS IS ALREADY ASKED UNDER ANOTHER WORD. sphere_high and sphere_low declare `facets: shown | hidden | only`, and those are platonic_grabbables' `plate | cast | armature` in the same order: fill with the triangle edges drawn over it, fill alone, edges alone. Both are implemented through the same grid shader's show_interior uniform. Two words, one question, four tokens - and neither declaration cites the other.

(6) THE MEASURED CLAIM, computed in a Python replica of this geometry at the sweep's own camera before the artifact was written. `resolution` bites hard when the deck is full and nearly stops when it is down to one body: mean focus over its six value pairs runs 30.07% at quorum=two, 24.67% at three, 20.35% at four and 7.21% at all. That fall is the truth line: at quorum=all the only thing standing is `cast`, and a poured body is the value that hides its own count, so refining the mould from 4 sides to 32 leaves the photograph almost alone. See dna.predicted_degeneracy, where it is written as a falsifiable ordering with a threshold.

(7) THE PIXEL METRIC PREFERRED THE PICTURE THAT SAYS THE WRONG THING, and it was caught by looking at the render rather than at the number. capsule and dome both cut a section by removing the near HALF on one plane. Rendered here, that half-body photographs as a flat pale slab standing on its pad - the cut face is the entire silhouette, no outer surface survives to say that a body was opened, and the tile reads as a cardboard cutout. Measured against the `cast` station drawn alone at resolution=mid it is also the STRONGER option: 16.21% focus for the half against 8.93% for a quarter-wedge cut. The quarter was taken anyway, at a cost of 7.28 points of station-level separation, because the half is a bigger number about a worse claim. This is Law 14 running in the other direction, and both numbers are recorded so the choice can be reversed by someone who disagrees.
dna.declines:
`facture` IS REFUSED AS THIS ARTIFACT'S VARYING AXIS, on the record, and the refusal is the design. There is no list to vary: five members, four vocabularies, one common term. Declaring a five-value `facture` axis here would be inventing a list the family does not have and then measuring it, which is the failure tools/check_dna_declarations.py exists to catch - except that a fabricated list assembled out of real members' real words would pass that gate, because every value would be a value some member declares. Under Law 2 the values are MIXED (one subtraction, two parallel apparatus - see dna.axis_shape), and a parallel set cannot be swept without dismantling three quarters of the exhibit, so the simultaneity is the object and something else varies. dna.kin records that the word is SAMPLED PER OBJECT rather than declared as a fixed list.

`tessellation` IS REFUSED AS THE NAME OF THE SECOND AXIS in favour of `resolution`. They are the same question with the same four integers - sphere_high.TESSELLATION is {coarse: 4, low: 7, high: 16, ultra: 32} and sphere_mid.RESOLUTION is {coarse: 4, mid: 7, fine: 16, ultra: 32}, identical numbers under different names for the middle two rungs. `resolution` is declared by four tokens (sphere_mid, riemann_pump, animated_noise_explorer, queer_marching_cave) against `tessellation`'s one, and sphere_mid is a primitive of this bench's own tier. The value list is taken character for character from sphere_mid, which is also where the numbers are read from at build time.

`facets` IS NOT ADOPTED, and it is the interesting decline. sphere_high and sphere_low declare `facets: shown | hidden | only`, which is platonic_grabbables' `plate | cast | armature` under a different word - the same three states, in the same order, both routed through the grid shader's show_interior uniform. It is recorded in dna.note (5) as a finding about how wide the pool really is, and it is not adopted as a station name because this bench exhibits the terms rather than switching between them, and `facture` is the word four of the five members that carry the argument actually use.

TIME IS REFUSED. The strongest unbuilt axis on this family is WHEN a state of making is shown - a mould filling, a wire frame being skinned, a body opening under a cut. Every value of it is a fact about a sequence and the evidence here is ONE STILL PNG per value, so a still would photograph the shutter and not the axis. info_board was swept across five duration exports and produced six identical tiles; declined rather than shipped as a finished-looking experiment.

GRABBING IS REFUSED. Three of the five members are grabbable and this bench is not. A pickable body is a body a visitor can hold up against another, which is a real and better version of this argument in VR - and it is also a body whose material_override gets swapped on pickup and drop, which is the one thing that would make two stations photograph as each other. The bench is a still exhibit; the family remains the place you can pick the argument up.

TEXT IS REFUSED. There is not one Label3D and not one glyph in any tile. A station is identified by what it draws, which is the whole of the word - a caption saying "armature" over a wire cage would let a visitor read the bench without looking at it. LabelFramer therefore has nothing to hang panels behind and nothing enters or leaves the capture AABB on that account.

A SIXTH STATION WAS CONSIDERED AND REFUSED. `wear` is the most vivid term in the pool and capsule implements it well (a deterministic position hash denting the skin). It is declared by ONE member. Standing it would have made a better photograph and a false claim about what the family shares.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, in the critic's own currency and not in changed pixels, because a prediction in the wrong units is a prediction about a different instrument. The critic crops to the union of the two frames' subject boxes, neutralises each frame's own corner background, converts to greyscale, RESIZES TO 160 x 160 and takes the mean of the hottest 5% (1,280 samples). Every number below comes from rebuilding this exact geometry in Python and rasterising it at this exact camera - RES 760, FOV 34, YAW 0.62, PITCH -0.26, PAD 1.9, dna.framing 0.62 - with a z-buffer, the rig's own two directional lights (1.25 at -42/-35, 0.45 at -20/130), its ambient (0.62, 0.65, 0.72) at 0.55, its FILMIC curve and its background (0.055, 0.055, 0.070), then pushing the result through that same crop-neutralise-grey-resize-hottest-5% pipeline.

READ EVERY NUMBER AS A FLOOR. A flat rasteriser has one light per lamp, no shadows, no ambient occlusion, no specular and no antialiasing, and every prediction in this corpus that named a pair and a number has under-predicted, by 1.5x to 6.7x. IF THE SWEEP COMES BACK BELOW THESE NUMBERS, SOMETHING IS BROKEN.

THE CLOSEST PAIR ON THE SHEET IS `resolution` fine <-> ultra, PREDICTED 4.62% FOCUS (0.30% frame), mean over the four quorum contexts: 7.76% at two, 6.08% at three, 4.12% at four, 0.51% at all. THE ARITHMETIC: 16 sides against 32 sides. On the `cast` station the difference is only the silhouette polygon - the sagitta of a chord at radius 0.10 m is r(1 - cos(pi/n)), which is 0.00192 m at n=16 and 0.00048 m at n=32, so the outline moves 0.45 px and the shading not at all, because normals are analytic and identical. On `facet` the checker halves in cell size from 12.3 px to 6.2 px, which changes a large area but at a spatial frequency the critic's 3.6x downsample to 160 x 160 averages away. On `armature` the edge count doubles while the tube diameter stays fixed at 5.0 px, so the OPEN gap between adjacent wires falls from 12.3 - 5.0 = 7.3 px to 6.2 - 5.0 = 1.2 px. On `shell` the crease splay falls from 0.98 px to 0.49 px, both sub-pixel. Four of the five stations are already past the point where more subdivision is visible, which is the axis's own claim about itself.

THE SPECIFIC TILE PAIR (all, fine) <-> (all, ultra) IS PREDICTED AT 0.51%, WHICH IS A TWIN AND IS THE POINT. At quorum=all exactly one body stands and it is `cast`; a poured body between 16 and 32 sides is the same photograph. If that pair comes back large, `cast` is not hiding its own count and the truth line on this artifact is wrong.

THE CLOSEST PAIR ON THE FIRST AXIS IS `quorum` three <-> four, predicted 30.50% focus (1.53% frame) - the two values that differ by a single body, `facet`, which covers roughly 4,679 px of a 129,920 px subject box - the measured drop in whole-frame subject share between those two tiles is 0.81 points.

A SECOND PREDICTION, STRONGER BECAUSE IT IS AN ORDERING AND NOT A NUMBER. The `resolution` axis must get WEAKER as `quorum` rises, monotonically over all four values, because every term the quorum removes is a term whose picture depends on how finely the body is cut, and the one term that survives to the end is the one that does not. Predicted means over the six resolution pairs: 30.07% at quorum=two, 24.67% at three, 20.35% at four, 7.21% at all. THE FALSIFYING THRESHOLDS: (a) the four means must fall strictly in that order, and (b) the ratio of the last to the first must stay below 0.50 - it is 0.240 in the replica, and the real render's shadows and specular will lift the `cast` end, so 0.50 is the bar at which the claim fails rather than merely loosens. If the ordering inverts anywhere, the two axes are entangled through something other than the standing terms and the bench is measuring its own deck.

AND ONE PAIR PREDICTED **NOT** TO BE DEGENERATE, because it looks as though it should be. `quorum` four <-> all differ by one body out of a five-pad deck and are the obvious twin candidate on a 16-tile sheet. Predicted 32.16% focus, well clear of the critic's 6% twin bar - because the body that leaves is `armature`, the only station rendered unshaded, and it is the brightest object in the frame. Removing it changes the hottest pixels far more than removing a shaded body of the same size would; note that its four per-context numbers run 19.32 / 32.79 / 38.12 / 38.42, so at coarse - where the cage is open and mostly background - it is nearly half what it is at ultra.

AXIS MEANS PREDICTED, over the 24 same-axis pairs each: `quorum` frame 4.14% / focus 48.03% -> BITES. `resolution` frame 1.35% / focus 20.57% -> BITES. Widest pair on the sheet: `quorum` two <-> all at 60.06%. If either axis mean comes back under the critic's 12% WEAK bar, read dna.still_note before the design: the two candidates are a --max below 16, which would publish a verdict about two values as a verdict about four, and a --staged run, which would put a plinth under a bench that brings its own deck.
dna.framing_why:
DERIVED FROM THE UNION AABB ACROSS ALL SIXTEEN VARIANTS, not from the default. Union 1.980 x 0.376 x 0.400 (x = deck end to deck end; y = deck underside 0.000 to the top of the body at 0.368 plus the shell's outward half-wall of 0.008; z = deck back to deck front), diagonal sqrt(3.9204 + 0.141376 + 0.16) = sqrt(4.221776) = 2.054696, radius 1.027348. The rig is dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) x PAD x framing with FOV 34 and PAD 1.9, so framing 1.0 would put the camera at 1.027348 / 0.3057307 x 1.9 = 6.3846 m and show a 3.904 m frame around a 1.98 m object - PAD 1.9 already shows 1.9x the bounding-sphere radius, which is why a bench object wants framing well below 1.0.

AT 0.62 the camera comes to 3.9584 m and the frame at the subject's centre depth to 2.4204 m, which is 313.99 px per metre. Rasterised at that setting, the subject's bounding box is IDENTICAL IN ALL SIXTEEN TILES at x 119..699, y 296..520 - because the deck is the widest and the tallest-spanning thing in every frame and it never changes - giving margins of 119 px left, 61 px right, 296 px top and 240 px bottom.

THAT IS A SPARSE SUBJECT, NOT A SMALL ONE, and the distinction is taxonomy_hall's and selection_garden's. The bounding box spans 580 px = 76.3% of frame width but only 22.5% of frame AREA, and the subject fills between 27.8% and 45.7% of that box depending on how many bodies are standing, so the whole-frame subject share runs 6.25% (quorum=all, coarse) to 10.28% (quorum=two, ultra). A deck with one body on it and four bare pads IS mostly deck. The critic's blank-render bar is BLANK_SUBJECT = 0.002 and floating_sphere_field is a legitimate artifact at 0.83%. DO NOT TIGHTEN THIS FRAMING ON SUBJECT SHARE ALONE.

TWO OTHER VALUES WERE MEASURED AND REJECTED. 0.60 gives 324.4 px/m but leaves about 50 px of margin on the RIGHT, which is the near end of an obliquely-viewed row and therefore the magnified one; instruction_bench rejected 51 px there and accepted 63. 0.64 gives 71 px of right margin at 304 px/m, which drops the ultra facet cell to 6.0 px and the shell splay at fine to 0.95 px for a margin nobody needs. 0.62 is the value where the tight margin is 61 px and nothing that carries meaning has fallen under 5 px.

GAUGE CHECK AT 313.99 px/m, because foresight_range shipped a bench's 0.028 m arrows onto an 18 m lane and sorting_hall drew a whole axis three pixels wide. Body 0.200 m wide -> 62.8 px (a lathed body of revolution projects its full diameter from any horizontal standpoint, so this is not foreshortened); body 0.310 m tall -> 97.3 px in world, 94.9 px in screen y at this pitch. Deck 0.050 m thick -> 15.7 px. Pad 0.230 m across -> 72.2 px, standing 0.008 m proud -> 2.5 px in height but reading as a 18.6 px ellipse from a camera pitched 14.9 degrees down, which is what makes an EMPTY pad legible. Slot pitch 0.400 m -> 125.6 px against a 62.8 px body, so adjacent bodies are separated by a clear 62.8 px and adjacent pads by 53.4 px; nothing on this deck occludes anything else.

FACET CELL WIDTH BY VALUE, which is the whole of the second axis: 2*pi*R/n = 49.3 px at coarse (n=4), 28.2 px at mid (7), 12.3 px at fine (16), 6.2 px at ultra (32). The ladder is chosen by the instrument, not by taste - it runs from a cell nobody can miss to a cell at the edge of what a 760 px tile can resolve - and the numbers behind it are sphere_mid's, not this bench's.

CAPSULE'S WIRE GAUGE SURVIVED THE SCALE CHANGE AND THE OTHER THREE DID NOT. capsule.gd::WIRE_RADIUS is 0.008 m, authored against a 0.25 m-radius body; here a three-sided tube of that radius is 0.016 m across = 5.02 px, exactly the legibility floor, so it is read from capsule and used unchanged. folded_strip's SHELL_THICKNESS 0.06 m is 1.5% of its 4 m strip; the same fraction of this 0.31 m body is 0.0047 m = 1.5 px, so it was RE-GAUGED to 0.016 m - the same one legibility unit, defined once as MARK and read twice. Transcribing the family's number would have drawn the entire shell station at one and a half pixels.
dna.still_note:
WHAT SHOULD BITE AND WHAT SHOULD NOT, said in advance so a thin number is read correctly.

THE DECK AND THE FIVE PADS ARE CONSTANT ACROSS BOTH AXES, BY CONSTRUCTION. They are built before either value is consulted, they are the widest and tallest-spanning geometry in every tile, and they are what fixes the camera. An empty pad is not a gap in the render - it is a station whose term did not meet the quorum, and it is drawn so that absence is legible rather than ambiguous.

THE `cast` STATION STANDS AT EVERY VALUE OF BOTH AXES. It is the only term all five members declare, so it survives every quorum threshold, and it is the term whose picture is least sensitive to resolution. A future reader who crops to the leftmost pad and reports `resolution` INERT there will have measured the argument and called it a bug: the predicted number for that station alone between fine and ultra is a 0.45 px silhouette shift and nothing else.

THE `armature` STATION IS THE ONLY UNSHADED ONE, following capsule.gd::_vertex_mat(true). It is therefore the brightest object in the frame and it carries more of the hottest-5% metric than its area suggests. That is why `quorum` four <-> all is predicted at 32.16% rather than at the twin bar - the body that leaves is the bright one - and it is stated here rather than discovered as a surprise.

THE Z-STACK, because a frame is four rails and not a slab. Deck y 0.000-0.050 spanning z -0.200..+0.200, UNDER everything. Pads y 0.050-0.058 lying on it, radius 0.115 at each of five slots. Bodies y 0.058-0.368, radius 0.100, one per occupied slot. Nothing is ever in front of anything else: the slot pitch is 0.400 m = 125.6 px against a 62.8 px body silhouette, and the pads clear each other by 53.4 px. The section station's two cut faces lie ON the planes x = cx and z = 0 through its own axis, so they are inside their own body's silhouette by construction and cannot occlude a neighbour.

DETERMINISM. No randf, no randomize, no _process, no _physics_process, no Timer, no Tween, no physics body, no shader time. The five source files are read once at build time and the whole scene is a function of (quorum, resolution). Two runs are byte-identical.

THE CAPTURE AABB IS THE REAL BODY. Every drawn node is a MeshInstance3D holding a SurfaceTool mesh - six of them at quorum=two, two at quorum=all. There is no MultiMeshInstance3D, no CSG, no particle system and no Label3D, so no `layers = 0` anchor is needed and none is present.

IF IT COMES BACK FAINT, CHECK THREE THINGS BEFORE THE DESIGN.
(1) Was --max at least 16? At the gallery's default cap of 9 a 4x4 declaration renders 4x2 and `resolution` is measured on {coarse, mid} alone - which would return a LARGE number (predicted 28.46%) rather than a faint one, but it would be a verdict about two values published as a verdict about four, and it would silently discard the predicted closest pair.
(2) Was the sweep run --staged? A 1.98 m bench is well under the 6 m staging cut-off, so a plinth would be added under it, the pair AABB would grow and every mark would shrink. This artifact brings its own deck; it does not want another.
(3) Is the standpoint doing the work?
